mainTopic: The decrees against the כותים, and whether a mixture containing דמאי is permitted.
overview: The גמרא first proves that רבי זירא accepted the report that רבן גמליאל forbade a כותי's שחיטה even when a Jew watches. It then explains why the decree was made. After an old man warned רבי שמעון בן אלעזר with a פסוק, רבי מאיר decreed against the כותים, because some of them worshipped a dove image on הר גריזים, and he takes a minority into account. The גמרא also explains that the plain meaning of that פסוק is about a student sitting before his teacher. Later, רבי אמי and רבי אסי made the כותים 'complete גוים'. Their ban on שחיטה and wine was finally accepted, and 'complete גוים' also means they lose a Jew's power to give up courtyard rights on שבת. Then רבי זירא sees רב אסי eat eggs cooked in wine and proves that a ready-made mixture with דמאי is permitted. The amud ends by answering challenges from a ברייתא about leaven and spices and from a משנה about a mother-in-law who swaps food.

steps.title: Proof that רבי זירא accepted the report about רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: If רבי זירא had rejected the report, he could easily have answered his own question by splitting the cases. Since he didn't, he must have accepted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think רבי זירא did not accept what he was told, he should have answered: here a Jew was standing over the כותי, and there no Jew was standing over him. So we must say he accepted it. Yes, learn that from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רבי זירא accepted the report that רבן גמליאל forbade a כותי's שחיטה even when a Jew is watching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was an easy way to fit רבי יוחנן's eating together with רבן גמליאל's ban: say one case had a Jew watching and the other did not. רבי זירא did not use that easy answer. That only makes sense if he accepted that the ban applies even when a Jew is watching, so the easy answer was no longer possible.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you were to think)
Let him answer it (for himself)
Standing over him (watching him)
He accepted it from him
Learn from it (this proves it)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן גמליאל and his court, a כותי's שחיטה is forbidden even when a Jew stands over him, and רבי זירא accepted this.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that he did not accept it from him,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי זירא, and "him" is רבי יעקב בר אידי, who told him about רבן גמליאל's ban.

phrases.english: let him answer it for himself:
here, when a Jew is standing over him,

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן כְּשֶׁאֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹמֵד עַל גַּבָּיו?
phrases.english: there, when a Jew is not standing over him?
Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this
that he accepted it from him.
Indeed, learn it from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּיךְ לָא קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion (from before this section) about רבי זירא and רבי יעקב בר אידי.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי זירא accepted the report that the decree applies even when a Jew stands over the כותי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי זירא's silence: he did not use the easy answer of splitting the cases.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי זירא accepted it, so the decree applies even with a Jew watching.

steps.title: Why did the Rabbis decree against the כותים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the decree forbidding a כותי's שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason the Rabbis made a decree against them?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the decree is clear, the גמרא asks why the Rabbis made it. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the כותים were treated as trustworthy in some areas. The גמרא wants to know what changed so that the Rabbis decided to forbid their שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: They decreed (made a rabbinic ban)
Against them (the כותים)
The Rabbis (here, רבן גמליאל and his court)

phrases.english: And what is the reason
that the Rabbis decreed against them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the decree just confirmed and asks for its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the decree against the כותים' שחיטה.

steps.title: The story of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and the wine of the כותים
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר sent his student to get wine from the כותים. An old man warned him with a פסוק, and after hearing this רבי מאיר decreed against them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like the story of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. רבי מאיר sent him to bring wine from the כותים. A certain old man met him and said: "Put a knife to your throat if you are a man of appetite." רבי שמעון בן אלעזר went and told this to רבי מאיר, and רבי מאיר decreed against them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a story that shows how the decree started: an old man hinted that the כותים could not be trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old man used a פסוק from משלי as a warning: hold yourself back and don't take their wine. When רבי מאיר heard this, he understood that the כותים had a problem and made a decree against them.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent him
Wine
The כותים (Samaritans)
An old man (an elder)
A person with a strong appetite

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: Like this incident with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar:
Rabbi Meir sent him
to bring wine from the area of the Kutim.
A certain old man found him
and said to him: "And put a knife to your throat
phrases.notes: משלי 23:2. He is hinting: hold yourself back and don't take their wine.

phrases.english: if you are a man of appetite."
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar went
and told the matter before Rabbi Meir,
and he decreed against them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The decree began with רבי מאיר, after an old man warned that the כותים could not be trusted.

steps.title: Why were the כותים not trusted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what was wrong with the כותים that led to the warning and the decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The story showed that the כותים were suspect, but it did not say why. The גמרא asks for the reason, setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old man's warning was only a hint. The גמרא wants the actual problem that made the כותים untrustworthy.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Digs deeper into the story of step 3.

steps.title: A dove idol on הר גריזים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that an image of a dove was found on top of הר גריזים, and the כותים there worshipped it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: they found an image of a dove at the top of הר גריזים, which they used to worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason: some כותים were caught worshipping an idol shaped like a dove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who worships עבודה זרה cannot be trusted with שחיטה or with wine. So the כותים who served this dove lost their trust.

keyTerms.meaning: The image of a dove
Mount Gerizim, the כותים' holy mountain
Worship (as עבודה זרה)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
They found that they had the image of a dove
at the top of Mount Gerizim,
which they would worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק דְּמוּת יוֹנָה מָצְאוּ לָהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כותים on הר גריזים worshipped a dove image.

steps.title: Why the whole group was banned because of a few
steps.stepSummary: Only a minority of כותים lived on הר גריזים, but רבי מאיר takes the minority into account, so he banned everyone. רבן גמליאל's court agrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר follows his own view that he is concerned about a minority, so he decreed on the majority because of the minority. And רבן גמליאל and his court also hold like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the decree covers all כותים even though only some worshipped the dove: רבי מאיר worries about a minority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most כותים did not live on הר גריזים, so one could ask why they were all forbidden. The answer is רבי מאיר's known approach: he takes a minority into account, so he banned the majority because of the minority. The גמרא adds that רבן גמליאל's court agrees, which explains why their decree from step 1 follows this approach.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning (his known view elsewhere)
He takes the minority into account
He decreed on the majority because of the minority
They hold (this view)

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on all כותים comes from רבי מאיר's view of taking a minority into account. Some on הר גריזים worshipped a dove, so all were forbidden, and רבן גמליאל's court holds the same way.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think most כותים worshipped the dove. Only a minority did. The ban covers everyone because רבי מאיר takes that minority into account.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir follows his own reasoning,
that he is concerned about the minority,
and he decreed on the majority because of the minority.
And Rabban Gamliel and his court
also hold like Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unstated question raised by step 5: why ban all כותים if only some worshipped the dove?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties the decree to a known general approach of רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the כותים on הר גריזים, a minority, should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since רבי מאיר takes a minority into account, all כותים are included, and רבן גמליאל's court agrees.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The decree against the כותים rests on taking the minority into account.

steps.title: What does the פסוק plainly mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the plain meaning is of the פסוק the old man used.
steps.simpleTranslation: The plain meaning of the פסוק: about what is it written?
steps.whatsHappening: The old man used the פסוק as a hint about the כותים. Now the גמרא asks what the פסוק itself is really talking about, setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old man borrowed "put a knife to your throat" for his own warning. The גמרא wants to know the פסוק's own simple meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: The plain meaning of the פסוק
About what is it written?

phrases.english: The plain meaning of the verse:
about what is it written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the פסוק quoted in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The simple subject of the פסוק in משלי.

steps.title: The פסוק is about a student before his teacher
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is about a student sitting before his teacher, as רבי חייא teaches from the full verses in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is about a student sitting before his teacher, as רבי חייא teaches: "When you sit to eat with a ruler, consider well what is before you; and put a knife to your throat, if you are a man of appetite."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the plain meaning of the פסוק is about how a student should act in front of his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא quotes the verse before it, about sitting before a "ruler". This shows the context: when you sit before your teacher, think carefully and hold yourself back.

keyTerms.meaning: A student sitting before his teacher
A ruler
Consider carefully
Your throat

phrases.english: About a student sitting before his teacher,
as Rabbi Chiya teaches:
"When you sit to eat with a ruler,
phrases.notes: משלי 23:1–2. In this reading the "ruler" is the teacher.

phrases.english: consider well what is before you;
and put a knife to your throat,
if you are a man of appetite."

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּתַלְמִיד הַיּוֹשֵׁב לִפְנֵי רַבּוֹ דְּתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק plainly speaks of a student sitting before his teacher, based on רבי חייא's teaching of the verses together.

steps.title: How a student should treat his teacher
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes explaining the פסוק. If the teacher can answer, ask him. If not, hold back so you don't embarrass him, or else leave him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a student knows his teacher can answer him with a reason, then 'בין': ask and learn. If not, 'understand who is before you and put a knife to your throat'. 'If you are a man of appetite', separate from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי חייא's explanation of the פסוקים in משלי, showing what each phrase means for a student sitting before his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is split into two cases. If the teacher can give reasons, the student should ask freely. If the teacher cannot, the student must hold back his questions so he does not shame him. If the student badly wants answers, he should find a different teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: To answer back with a reason, to explain why
Understand, seek wisdom (ask your questions)
A knife to your throat (hold yourself back from asking)
Separate yourself from him

steps.whatToRemember: The simple meaning of the פסוק is about a student and his teacher: ask a teacher who can answer, and don't embarrass one who can't.

phrases.english: If a student knows about his teacher
that he knows how to answer him with a reason,
"understand" (ask and learn from him).
And if not,
"understand who is before you,
and put a knife to your throat":
phrases.notes: משלי 23:1–2. In other words, stop yourself from asking questions he can't answer.

phrases.english: "if you are a man of appetite":
separate yourself from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם יוֹדֵעַ תַּלְמִיד בְּרַבּוֹ שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לְהַחֲזִיר לוֹ טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי חייא's reading of the פסוק that began in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches a student when to ask his teacher and when to hold back or leave.

steps.title: רבי אמי and רבי אסי make the כותים full גוים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו sends רבי יצחק בן יוסף to get wine from the כותים. An old man warns that they don't keep the Torah. The report goes up to רבי אמי and רבי אסי, who rule that the כותים are complete גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו sent רבי יצחק בן יוסף to bring wine from the place of the כותים. An old man met him and said: There are no Torah keepers here. רבי יצחק told רבי אבהו, and רבי אבהו told רבי אמי and רבי אסי. They did not leave until they made the כותים full גוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that ends with a new ruling: רבי אמי and רבי אסי declared the כותים to be complete גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, there were doubts about the כותים, but they were not treated fully as גוים. The old man's report that they do not keep the Torah led the חכמים to act right away and give them the full status of גוים. This ruling is what the next steps will question.

keyTerms.meaning: People who keep the Torah
They did not move from there (they acted at once)
Complete, full גוים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak ben Yosef:
Rabbi Abbahu sent him
to bring wine from the place of the Kutim.
A certain old man found him

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֵית כָּאן שׁוֹמְרֵי תוֹרָה.
phrases.english: and said to him: There are no keepers of the Torah here.
Rabbi Yitzchak went and told the matter
to Rabbi Abbahu,
and Rabbi Abbahu went and told the matter
to Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi,
and they did not move from there
until they made them complete gentiles.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן יוֹסֵף שַׁדְּרֵיהּ רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about the status of the כותים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אמי and רבי אסי ruled that the כותים are complete גוים.

steps.title: Wasn't this already decreed earlier?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the new ruling added. If it banned their שחיטה and wine, earlier חכמים had already decreed that.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what did they make them full גוים? If for שחיטה and יין נסך, the חכמים already decreed that against them back then!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story: the decree of רבי אמי and רבי אסי seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the דף we saw that רבי מאיר and the court of רבן גמליאל already banned the כותים. So if this new ruling was only about their שחיטה and their wine, nothing new was done. The question looks like 'for what?', but it really works as a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Kosher slaughter of an animal
Wine poured for עבודה זרה, which is forbidden
From back then (from that earlier time)

phrases.english: For what?
If for slaughter and libation wine,
the Rabbis already decreed against them from back then!
phrases.notes: This points back to the decree of רבי מאיר and רבן גמליאל's court that we saw earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of the ruling in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of רבי אמי and רבי אסי that the כותים are complete גוים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Banning their שחיטה and wine had already been decreed in earlier generations, so the new ruling seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The first decree was not accepted, the second one was
steps.stepSummary: The earlier חכמים did decree, but the people did not accept it. When רבי אמי and רבי אסי decreed, the people accepted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They decreed, but the people did not accept it from them. רבי אמי and רבי אסי came, decreed, and the people accepted it from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the new decree was needed because the old one never took hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling was not new in content, but it was new in effect. A decree that the people do not accept does not really work in practice. רבי אמי and רבי אסי made the same ban, and this time it was accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: And the people did not accept it from them
And the people did accept it from them

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי אמי and רבי אסי made a new rule about שחיטה and wine. That ban already existed; what was new is that this time the people accepted it. Step 14 shows that calling them 'complete גוים' also adds something new, in the courtyard laws of שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on the כותים' שחיטה and wine began with רבי מאיר and רבן גמליאל's court, but it only took hold in practice in the time of רבי אמי and רבי אסי.

phrases.english: They decreed,
but the people did not accept it from them.
Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi came,
decreed, and the people accepted it from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical distinction: same decree, but now accepted by the people
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling of רבי אמי and רבי אסי repeated an existing ban and added nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The earlier decree was not accepted. Only the decree of רבי אמי and רבי אסי was accepted and took effect.

steps.title: What does 'complete גוים' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase 'complete גוים' means in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'complete גוים' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact meaning of the phrase from the story. This sets up רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'complete' suggests the כותים are now treated like גוים even in areas beyond שחיטה and wine. The גמרא wants to know which area this is.

phrases.english: What is meant by "complete gentiles"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the phrase used in the story of step 10 to define it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical meaning of calling the כותים 'complete גוים'.

steps.title: Giving up and giving over rights in a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that 'complete גוים' refers to the laws of giving up and handing over rights in a shared courtyard on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is about giving up rights and handing over rights.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the כותים now have the status of גוים for the courtyard laws of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When people share a courtyard on שבת, one person's rights can stop the others from carrying. רב נחמן בר יצחק teaches that for giving up or handing over those rights, a כותי is now treated like a גוי and not like a Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: To give up one's rights (in a shared courtyard on שבת)
To hand over one's rights to others in the courtyard

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'complete גוים' goes beyond food. The כותים are treated like גוים even in the laws of carrying in a shared courtyard on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Complete גוים' means the כותים are like גוים for giving up and handing over rights in a shared courtyard on שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Regarding giving up rights
and handing over rights.
phrases.notes: This is about a courtyard shared by several people on שבת, where one person's rights affect whether the others may carry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לְבַטֵּל רְשׁוּת וְלִיתֵּן רְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Complete גוים' refers to the laws of giving up and handing over rights in a shared courtyard on שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a Jew who breaks שבת and courtyard rights
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a Jewish sinner who keeps שבת in public can give up or hand over his courtyard rights, but one who breaks שבת in public cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: a Jewish sinner who keeps his שבת in the marketplace can give up his rights and hand over his rights. One who does not keep his שבת in the marketplace cannot give up his rights or hand over his rights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב נחמן בר יצחק's explanation. It shows that the courtyard rules really depend on whether someone counts as a Jew or as a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Keeping or breaking שבת in public decides a person's status here. Someone who breaks שבת openly loses the Jewish ability to give up his courtyard rights. In the same way, calling the כותים 'complete גוים' means they lose this ability too.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jew who has turned away from keeping the Torah; a sinner
Keeps his שבת in the marketplace, meaning in public
Gives up his rights in the shared courtyard
Hands over his rights in the courtyard to someone else

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'marketplace' does not mean he only keeps שבת while shopping. It means he keeps שבת in public, where people can see.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source showing that publicly keeping שבת is what decides whether a person counts as a Jew for these courtyard rules.

phrases.english: And as it is taught in a ברייתא: a Jewish sinner
who keeps his שבת in the marketplace
phrases.notes: 'In the marketplace' means in public, where everyone can see.

phrases.english: can give up his rights and can hand over his rights
but one who does not keep his שבת in the marketplace
cannot give up his rights or hand over his rights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן בר יצחק's explanation that 'complete גוים' is about the courtyard rules.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that being treated like a גוי affects a person's ability to give up courtyard rights on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a Jew who breaks שבת in public

steps.title: The reason: a Jew gives up rights, but a גוי must be rented from
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that only a Jew can give up or hand over rights. With a גוי, the others must rent his share.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is because the חכמים said: a Jew can hand over his rights and give up his rights, but with a גוי, it does not work until they rent from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the reason for its rule. A Jew can give up his rights just by saying so, but a גוי's share has to be rented.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two different ways of handling a neighbor's share are set up here. A Jew uses ביטול רשות, simply giving up his rights. A גוי's share needs שכירות, a rental. The sinner who breaks שבת in public is placed in the גוי group.

keyTerms.meaning: Renting; here, renting the גוי's share of the courtyard
Until he rents (it does not work until the share is rented)

phrases.english: Because they said:
a Jew can hand over his rights and give up his rights
but with a גוי, it does not work until one rents from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the ברייתא's rule in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew can give up or hand over his courtyard rights; a גוי's share must be rented.

steps.title: How does a Jew give up his rights?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how a Jew actually hands over or gives up his rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is it done?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a short question to set up its next line. It wants to explain the actual method of giving up rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a Jew can give up his rights has been stated. Now the ברייתא asks what he actually has to do or say to make it work.

keyTerms.meaning: How? In what way?

phrases.english: How?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical method behind the rule just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What a Jew must do to give up or hand over his courtyard rights

steps.title: Saying the words is enough
steps.stepSummary: If he says 'my rights are acquired by you' or 'my rights are given up to you,' the other person acquires them with no formal act.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says to him: 'My rights are acquired by you,' or 'My rights are given up to you.' The other person has acquired them, and there is no need for a formal act of transfer.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. Simply saying the words is enough to give up or hand over the rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, transferring ownership needs a formal act of acquiring (a קנין). Here, words alone work. This easy method is what the open שבת-breaker, and so also the כותים, lose.

keyTerms.meaning: My rights are acquired by you
My rights are given up to you
To transfer something through a formal act of acquiring

steps.whatToRemember: A Jew gives up his courtyard rights just by saying so. A גוי's share must be rented. A Jew who breaks שבת in public, and the כותים once they were called 'complete גוים,' fall into the גוי group.

phrases.english: He says to him: 'My rights are acquired by you'
or 'My rights are given up to you,' and the other person has acquired them
and there is no need to transfer them through a formal act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how rights are given up.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Saying 'my rights are acquired by you' or 'given up to you' is enough; no formal act of transfer is needed.

steps.title: רבי זירא and רב אסי are served eggs cooked in wine
steps.stepSummary: At an inn in יאי, the two חכמים are served eggs cooked in wine. רבי זירא does not eat them, but רב אסי does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא and רב אסי happened to come to the inn of יאי. They were served eggs shriveled from being cooked in wine. רבי זירא did not eat, and רב אסי ate.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. Two חכמים are served the same food, and they act differently: one eats and one does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is the wine the eggs were cooked in. The story sets up a question about why רב אסי was not careful about it.

keyTerms.meaning: They happened to come to a place
An inn
Eggs that shrank and shriveled from cooking

phrases.english: רבי זירא and רב אסי
happened to come to the inn of יאי
They brought before them
eggs that had shriveled from being cooked in wine.
רבי זירא did not eat
and רב אסי ate.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא וְרַב אַסִּי אִיקְּלַעוּ לְפוּנְדְּקָא דְּיָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story, moving away from the courtyard rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: one חכם ate eggs cooked in wine at an inn, and the other did not.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks: aren't you worried about דמאי?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges רב אסי: weren't you worried the dish contained wine that might not have been tithed?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רב אסי: Is the Master not worried about a mixture containing דמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא questions why רב אסי ate. The wine might be דמאי, produce that may not have been tithed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine from an ordinary seller could be דמאי. Since the eggs were cooked in it, the whole dish is a mixture that may contain untithed wine. So רבי זירא's question is really a challenge to רב אסי's eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce bought from someone who may not have tithed it
A mixture
Worries about, is concerned about

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: רבי זירא said to רב אסי:
Is the Master not worried
phrases.notes: 'Master' is a polite way of saying 'you.'

phrases.english: about a mixture containing דמאי?
phrases.notes: The worry is that the wine in the dish was never tithed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אסי's choice to eat in the story just told.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's eating of the eggs cooked in wine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wine may be דמאי, so a dish cooked in it is a mixture that should be avoided.

steps.title: רב אסי: It did not cross my mind
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי answers that he simply did not think about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It did not enter my mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי admits he did not think about the דמאי problem. He is not defending his eating; he just forgot to consider it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי does not argue that the food was allowed. He admits he made a mistake by not paying attention, which leaves the story open to continue.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not on my mind; I did not think of it

phrases.english: He said to him: It did not enter my mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge by admitting he did not think of it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב אסי did not think about the דמאי issue at all; he admits it was an oversight.

steps.title: A צדיק would not be allowed to stumble
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reasons that it can't be that the חכמים forbade a mixture with דמאי, because then רב אסי would have eaten something forbidden, and הקדוש ברוך הוא protects צדיקים from that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Could it be that the חכמים made a decree against a mixture containing דמאי, and things worked out so that רב אסי ate something forbidden? If הקדוש ברוך הוא does not bring a mishap through the animals of צדיקים, then surely He does not bring one through the צדיקים themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא thinks to himself that רב אסי could not really have eaten something forbidden. So he guesses that a mixture containing דמאי must be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a קל וחומר: animals of צדיקים are protected from eating forbidden food, so צדיקים themselves are protected even more. That leads רבי זירא to suspect that a mixture with דמאי is not forbidden at all. Now he needs a source to back this up, and he looks for one in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A mishap; here, coming to eat something forbidden
All the more so (the end of a קל וחומר)
The animals of the righteous

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not saying רב אסי was allowed to be careless. He is saying that because רב אסי is a צדיק, the food was probably permitted to begin with, and he goes on to check this.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Is it possible that they decreed against a mixture containing demai,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִסְתַּיְּיעָא מִילְּתָא דְּרַב אַסִּי לְמֵיכַל אִיסּוּרָא?
phrases.english: and things worked out so that Rav Asi ate something forbidden?
phrases.notes: He means the eggs cooked in wine from step 19.

phrases.english: Now, if with the animals of the righteous

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵבִיא תַּקָּלָה עַל יָדָן,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not bring about a mishap through them,
then the righteous themselves, is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רב אסי's answer that he didn't think about it, and suggests the food was permitted anyway.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צדיק would not be led to eat something forbidden, so a mixture with דמאי is probably not forbidden.

steps.title: A ready-made mixture with דמאי is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא finds a ברייתא: someone who buys wine or beans to make a mixture must tithe them as דמאי, but the finished mixtures themselves are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא went out, looked carefully, and found the answer, as we learned: One who buys wine to put into fish brine or into אלונתית, vetch to make grist, or lentils to make groats, must tithe them because of דמאי, and certainly if they are surely untithed. But the finished mixtures themselves are permitted, because they are a mixture.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings a ברייתא that proves his idea. If you buy the plain ingredient, you must tithe it, but if you buy a finished mixture, it is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes a split. A person who buys wine or beans in order to mix them himself must tithe them as דמאי. But a finished mixture bought already made is permitted, since the doubtful item is only one part of it. That fits רב אסי's eggs cooked in wine, so he ate nothing forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He examined carefully and found
Fish brine or fish sauce
A drink made from wine mixed with other ingredients
Produce that is certainly untithed (טבל)
Obligated to tithe because of the doubt of דמאי

steps.whatToRemember: Buying the ingredient in order to mix it = tithe it as דמאי. A finished mixture bought ready-made = permitted. So רב אסי did nothing wrong.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira went out, examined carefully, and found,
as we learned:
One who buys wine to put into fish brine
or into aluntit,
phrases.notes: אלונתית is a drink made by mixing wine with other things.

phrases.english: vetch to make grist from it,
lentils to make groats from them –
he is obligated to tithe because of demai,
and needless to say, because of certainly untithed produce.
But they themselves are permitted,
phrases.notes: "They themselves" means the finished dishes, like the brine or the groats, bought already made.

phrases.english: because they are a mixture.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְפַק רַבִּי זֵירָא דַּק וְאַשְׁכַּח, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רבי זירא's guess from step 22 with a written source.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים did not forbid a mixture containing דמאי, so רב אסי's eggs cooked in wine were permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: finished mixtures like fish brine and aluntit are permitted "because they are a mixture."

steps.title: Challenge from dough and a pot given to a neighbor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: did they really not decree against a mixture with דמאי? It starts quoting a ברייתא about giving a neighbor dough to bake or a pot to cook.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that they did not decree against a mixture with דמאי? But it was taught: One who gives his neighbor dough to bake or a pot to cook does not need to worry about the leaven and spices in it, neither because of שביעית nor because of מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the proof from step 23 and starts bringing another ברייתא. This step is setting up the challenge, and its sharp point comes in the next lines of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new ברייתא is about leaven and spices, small parts of dough or a pot of food, which is the same kind of mixture case. The opening part shown here says the owner need not worry. The גמרא is quoting it as "והתניא," a challenge, so the rest of this ברייתא will show a case where the חכמים did worry about a mixture.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaven, the sourdough starter used to make dough rise
Spices
Produce of the seventh (שמיטה) year, which has special restrictions
Tithe
He does not need to worry

steps.confusionAlert: The words quoted so far sound like they agree with רבי זירא. The challenge comes from the continuation of the same ברייתא, so don't stop reading here.

phrases.english: And did they really not decree against a mixture containing demai?
But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
One who gives his neighbor dough to bake,
or a pot to cook –
he need not worry about the leaven and spices in it,
phrases.notes: The worry would be that she swapped his leaven or spices for her own.

phrases.english: neither because of the Sabbatical Year
nor because of tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא גָּזְרוּ עַל תַּעֲרוֹבֶת דְּמַאי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 23 that mixtures with דמאי were not decreed against.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from step 23 that a mixture containing דמאי is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא about leaven and spices mixed into dough or a pot seems, in its continuation, to treat such mixtures with concern, which would mean the חכמים did decree against them.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: worry about her leaven and spices
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes: if he tells the neighbor to use her own ingredients, he must worry that her leaven and spices are from שביעית or were never tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he said to her, 'Make it for me from your own,' he must be concerned about the leaven and spices in it, because of שביעית and because of מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the previous step. This last line is the actual challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her leaven and spices are mixed into his dough or pot, yet he still has to worry about them. That suggests the חכמים did forbid a mixture with דמאי, which contradicts רבי זירא's ברייתא from step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: Make it for me from your own (use your own ingredients)
He must be concerned, so he has to treat it as a doubt

phrases.english: And if he said to her: 'Make it for me from your own,'
he must be concerned about the leaven and spices in it
because of the Sabbatical year and because of tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָמַר לָהּ עֲשִׂי לִי מִשֶּׁלִּיכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quotation that step 24 began.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's conclusion that a mixture with דמאי is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her ingredients are only part of a mixture, yet he must still worry about them. So a mixture with דמאי seems to be forbidden.

steps.title: Asking her to use her own counts as mixing it himself
steps.stepSummary: That case is different. By telling her to use her ingredients, he is treated as if he mixed them in with his own hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there: since he told her, 'Make it for me from your own,' it is as if he mixed it in with his own hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer explaining why the leaven-and-spices case does not disprove רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency for mixtures applies when the mixture is already made. Here he himself asked for her ingredients to be put in, so it counts as his own deliberate mixing. In that situation the leniency does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; the case being cited is special
Mixing it in with one's own hands, meaning on purpose

phrases.english: It is different there,
since he said to her: 'Make it for me from your own,'
it is like someone who mixed it with his own hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: deliberate mixing versus an existing mixture
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that every mixture with דמאי is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a mixture he caused on purpose is forbidden. A mixture that is already made stays permitted.

steps.title: רפרם: leaven and spices give taste, and taste is not cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רפרם offers a different answer. Leaven and spices are added for flavor, and flavor never gets cancelled in a mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם said: Leaven and spices are different, because they are put in for taste, and taste is not nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם gives a second, separate answer to the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רפרם does not rely on who did the mixing. He focuses on the ingredients themselves. Leaven and spices are added to change the taste of the food, and something that gives taste does not disappear into the mixture, so the worry remains. Other ingredients mixed with דמאי would still be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Taste or flavor
Is not nullified; does not become cancelled out in the mixture

phrases.english: Rafram said:
Leaven and spices are different,
because they are made for giving taste,
and taste is not nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 25's challenge, offered instead of step 26's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the ingredients: things that give flavor
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids every mixture with דמאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only flavor-giving ingredients like leaven and spices stay forbidden, because taste is never cancelled out.

steps.title: Why not worry that she swapped his ingredients?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we trust that she did not swap his ingredients. It cites a משנה requiring a man to tithe food he gives his mother-in-law, because she may swap spoiled ingredients.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we are not concerned that she swapped them? But we learned in a משנה: One who gives food to his mother-in-law tithes what he gives her and what he takes back from her, because she is suspected of swapping what spoils!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to the ברייתא. Why are we not worried that the neighbor replaced his ingredients with her own?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes that when he gives her his own dough or pot, what comes back is still his. But a משנה says a mother-in-law is suspected of swapping, so everything must be tithed. Why not suspect the neighbor of the same thing?

keyTerms.meaning: Swapping or replacing one item with another
His mother-in-law
She is suspected
What gets spoiled or ruined

phrases.english: And are we not concerned about swapping?
But didn't we learn: One who gives to his mother-in-law
tithes what he gives her
and what he takes from her,
because she is suspected of swapping what spoils!
phrases.notes: If his food spoils while she is preparing it, she might quietly replace it with her own untithed food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the question of mixtures to a new worry about the neighbor in the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's assumption that when he uses his own ingredients, no worry exists
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה worries that a mother-in-law swaps ingredients, so we should worry about the neighbor too.

steps.title: The mother-in-law has a special reason to swap
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains that the mother-in-law is different. She wants her daughter to eat well and is embarrassed to tell her son-in-law that his food spoiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: There the reason is as it was taught: רבי יהודה said, she wants what is good for her daughter and is embarrassed before her son-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining why the mother-in-law, and not an ordinary neighbor, is suspected of swapping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about swapping is not general. It comes from the mother-in-law's family feelings: she wants her daughter to eat good food and is too embarrassed to admit that something spoiled. An ordinary neighbor has no such reason, so the ברייתא need not worry about her.

keyTerms.meaning: Her daughter's well-being
She is embarrassed
Her son-in-law

steps.whatToRemember: A mixture with דמאי is permitted. The leaven-and-spices case is an exception, either because he asked for her ingredients (which counts as mixing it himself) or, per רפרם, because taste is never cancelled. We worry about swapping only when there is a special motive, like a mother-in-law's.

phrases.english: There, the reason is as it was taught:
Rabbi Yehuda said:
She wants what is good for her daughter
and is embarrassed before her son-in-law.
phrases.notes: She would rather swap in her own food than tell him his food was ruined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case by a special motive
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone preparing food for another person is suspected of swapping.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the mother-in-law is suspected, because of her feelings for her daughter and her embarrassment before her son-in-law.
